title: On the road
intro: Driving, road signs and the words you need when something goes wrong. See unit 8 and unit 41 for the town itself, unit 22 for the journey.

entries.note: la autopista is a motorway, usually with a toll (la cuota or el peaje).
A real ambiguity: in Mexico el camión is the bus. Elsewhere it is a lorry.

ex.en: The lorry was blocking the street.
I took the bus to Puebla.

entries.note: la bici and la moto are the everyday short forms. la moto is feminine, short for la motocicleta.
el buque is a large vessel; la lancha a small motorboat.
la llanta in Latin America, el neumático in Spain. la rueda is the wheel.
frenar is to brake; acelerar to accelerate.

ex.en: Don't let go of the steering wheel.

entries.note: el límite de velocidad is the speed limit; rápido and lento are fast and slow.
chocar is to crash; el choque the crash.

ex.es: Hubo un accidente en la curva.
ex.en: There was an accident on the bend.

entries.note: la licencia de conducir or el permiso de conducir is a driving licence.
Masculine despite the -a. el plano is a street plan.

ex.en: Look for it on the map.

entries.note: el chofer in Latin America, especially of a hired driver.

ex.es: El conductor no vio la señal.
ex.en: The driver didn't see the sign.

entries.note: tomar asiento is to take a seat; el cinturón the seatbelt.
The two words on every airport board.

ex.es: La llegada está prevista a las seis.
La salida se retrasó una hora.
ex.en: Departure was delayed by an hour.

entries.note: Singular and uncountable, like la ropa. la maleta is the case — see unit 22.
declarar is to declare; la frontera the border.

ex.en: We crossed the border at night.

entries.note: volar is to fly; la escala a stopover; despegar and aterrizar to take off and land.

ex.es: El vuelo hace una escala en Bogotá.
ex.en: The flight has a stopover in Bogotá.

entries.note: In Mexico el taxista is the taxi driver.

ex.en: We ordered a taxi by phone.
